THE_STRONGER_EVIDENCE_pages_1280_1296_ar.claim: The vault's original citation placed a paper at JEP:Learning Memory and Cognition 18(6), 1280-1296.
THE_STRONGER_EVIDENCE_pages_1280_1296_ar.finding: I enumerated every Crossref record Crossref holds for that journal's volume 18 issue 6 (18 records, deduplicated to 11 distinct articles). The claimed range is FULLY OCCUPIED by other papers: Bentin, Moscovitch & Heth at 1270-1283 covers 1280-1283, and Light, LaVoie & Valencia-Laver at 1284-1297 covers 1284-1296. No gap exists, and no Bjork paper appears anywhere in the issue.
THE_STRONGER_EVIDENCE_pages_1280_1296_ar.why_this_matters: A 404 alone only shows the identifier is not registered -- it cannot show the claimed ARTICLE never existed. Page occupancy is the same kind of proof that settled the fabricated Anderson 1991 paper: another paper demonstrably sits on the pages the citation claims. This closes the question that a 404 left open.

Bjork_1992_VERIFIED_AND_STRENGTHENED.no_1991_version_exists: The '1991' often attached to the two-strength account is a mis-citation of this 1992 chapter. PubMed holds 18 Bjork papers in Memory & Cognition spanning 1973-2026 and none from 1991; the commonly cited location 19(5) 594-605 does not resolve (10.1037/0278-7393.19.5.594 -> 404) and the articles in that volume slot are unrelated.
Bjork_1992_VERIFIED_AND_STRENGTHENED.no_doi_and_that_is_verified_not_assumed: Crossref holds no record for this title and OpenAlex returns doi=None. It is a 1992 Erlbaum print chapter, predating widespread DOI registration. The vault now cites it WITHOUT an identifier, stating so explicitly. Attaching a plausible-looking DOI would have recreated the exact error being repaired.

VERIFIER_BUG_FOUND_AND_FIXED.fix: The character class now permits a balanced <...::AID-...> suffix and a trailing ;<digits>-<digits> SICI tail, while still stopping at genuine HTML. Verified against four cases: plain DOI, DOI containing parentheses (10.1016/S0079-7421(08)60536-8), full SICI, and an HTML anchor.
VERIFIER_BUG_FOUND_AND_FIXED.lesson: A correct vault entry can be made to look fabricated by a parser bug. Before concluding that an identifier is wrong, check whether the extraction itself is losing characters -- especially for publishers whose identifier syntax uses the delimiters a regex would naturally exclude.
VERIFIER_BUG_FOUND_AND_FIXED.regression_pinned_by: tests/test_t2_sici_doi.py (5 tests). The test was written FIRST and confirmed to fail against the old pattern before the fix was applied, so it is a real regression test rather than a description of current behaviour.
VERIFIER_BUG_FOUND_AND_FIXED.root_cause: verify_t2_titles.py's DOI and URL regexes excluded '<' and '>' from the identifier body, to avoid swallowing HTML markup. But Wiley SICI DOIs are delimited by exactly those characters: 10.1002/(SICI)1099-0720(1998120)12:6<617::AID-ACP542>3.0.CO;2-5. Cut at the '<', the regex emitted 10.1002/(SICI)1099-0720(1998120)12:6, which cannot resolve in any registry -- a guaranteed 404 indistinguishable from a fabricated citation.
VERIFIER_BUG_FOUND_AND_FIXED.summary: The Encoding-Specificity row was NOT a vault defect. The vault was correct in both the frontmatter and the reference entry; the verifier was truncating the identifier.

Rouder_and_Morey_2005_FABRICATED.action: Reference struck and the real occupant of those pages recorded in its place, so the next reader can see what the identifier actually pointed at. The body claim that rested on it is retained and marked unverified.
Rouder_and_Morey_2005_FABRICATED.finding: No such paper exists. The pages the file claimed -- Psychological Review 112(4) 842-855 -- are actually 841-861, occupied by Johnson, M.R. & Busemeyer, J.R., 'A dynamic, stochastic, computational model of preference reversal phenomena', 10.1037/0033-295x.112.4.841, which RESOLVES. The file's '...842' is the neighbouring article, which is why it never returned anything. Two targeted Crossref searches for a Rouder & Morey paper of that title, and for any signal-detection decomposition of the picture-superiority effect, returned no such work.

the_nine_uncited_dead_sources_REMOVED.no_substitutes_invented: Bibliographic searches were run per topic, but a bare DOI with no title does not record what was meant, so no attribution was guessed. This matches the standing instruction that unresolved disagreement is acceptable but fabrication is not.
the_nine_uncited_dead_sources_REMOVED.safety: A pre-flight check confirmed each had body=0 and frontmatter=1 BEFORE any write, and the script aborts if that is ever untrue. Every removal is annotated in-file with a dated HTML comment naming the count, the reason, and this file.

method_and_why_the_first_answers_were_vo.structural_finding_about_the_nine: All 9 unattributable DOIs appear ZERO times outside the frontmatter: no title, no author, no reference-list entry, and no body sentence depends on any of them. They are uncited scaffolding, not mis-citations, which is why removing them orphans nothing -- unlike McCloskey, which WAS body-cited and had to be repaired.
method_and_why_the_first_answers_were_vo.the_method_that_actually_resolved_things: Stop probing identifiers and search for the PAPER. A file can hold a real work under a wrong identifier -- the McCloskey row is exactly that case -- so deletion-by-404 would have destroyed genuine sources. Searching for the work found two real papers the 404s had hidden.
method_and_why_the_first_answers_were_vo.the_verifier_defines_the_verdict: verify_t2_titles.py's own docstring: 'unresolvable -- could not check. Stays medium. NOT counted as match.' A 404 is therefore a COVERAGE verdict, never a nonexistence verdict. Every row here was re-adjudicated on that basis.
method_and_why_the_first_answers_were_vo.three_routes_each_proved_live_first: Crossref, OpenAlex and doi.org (CSL content negotiation) were each probed against two known-good control DOIs -- 10.1037/0278-7393.20.5.1063 and 10.1038/35066572 -- and all three returned 200 on both before any target was read. Only then were the 15 tested. Result: 0 of 15 resolved on any route.
two_instruments_failed_and_were_discarde: A first multiroute script reported '0 of 15 resolved' with EMPTY route dicts, which is indistinguishable from the script aborting. Re-probing the routes by hand showed three of them live at HTTP 200, so that run was a broken instrument and its result was void, not a finding.

A bibliographic sweep crashed on a Crossref record with a null author (TypeError in a str.join), and its PubMed control returned 0 for the query 'Anderson BJ[au] AND Bjork RA[au]' -- 'BJ' is not a PubMed initials form, so the control was malformed. Both the crash and the control were fixed and the sweep re-run; it then returned the real Anderson 1994 record as its own control.
